partners.diseaseBName: congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia
partners.mechanism_chain: SPTLC2 (HGNC:11157) —DISRUPTS→ de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006660); de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006660) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defects (HP:0001627); PRKD1 (HGNC:9742) —DISRUPTS→ sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006660); sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006660) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001051); de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006660) —BINDS→ sphingolipid metabolism (GO:0006660). Loss-of-function mutations in SPTLC2 disrupt de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis, leading to congenital heart defects. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PRKD1 disrupt broader sphingolipid metabolism, contributing to ectodermal dysplasia. The hypothesis proposes that these distinct but related disruptions converge on the shared pathway of sphingolipid metabolism, creating a common downstream cellular environment that manifests as distinct but potentially overlapping phenotypes.

falsification.text: If genetic studies demonstrate that mutations in SPTLC2 and PRKD1 lead to entirely independent and non-interacting molecular pathways with no shared downstream effectors or metabolites, and if no patients with mutations in one gene show any phenotypic overlap with the other disease, this hypothesis would be falsified. Specifically, if evidence emerges that the disrupted sphingolipid metabolic pathways are completely distinct and do not influence each other's downstream consequences.
falsification.gnomad_variant: The absence of pathogenic variants in SPTLC2 and PRKD1 in gnomAD databases would not falsify this hypothesis, as these are rare diseases.
